title: Mother Maria Skobtsova
hookLine: an Orthodox nun in Paris hides Jews and dies in Ravensbrück

lines: A NUN AT THE DAWN MARKET.
A HOUSE FULL OF THE UNWANTED.
cards: A nun in a black habit is haggling at a Paris market at dawn, buying the cheap end of the vegetables, then hauling the sacks back through the streets herself.

She has been a poet, a revolutionary, a mayor in her old Russian town, a wife twice, a mother. Her house on the rue de Lourmel is full of people nobody else wants: the homeless, the drunk, the broke, the mentally ill.
Some of the church people are scandalized. A nun should be in a monastery, praying. She thinks she is praying.

teach.h: A NUN WHOSE MONASTERY WAS THE WORLD.
teach.b: She was born Elizaveta in the Russian Empire and left after the revolution, like other Russians who became refugees in Paris. After the death of one of her children, her life turned.
She became an Orthodox nun, Mother Maria, but with her bishop's blessing she lived in the city, not behind walls. Her monastery, she liked to say, was the whole world. Her idea was simple and hard.

Every person is an image of God, an icon. Orthodox Christians honor icons in church: they kiss them, bow to them, light candles before them. So why not bow to the living icon in front of you, the hungry man at the door?
Today's line, the sacrament of the brother, is a phrase people link with her: the altar is holy, and so is your brother.
The First Letter of John puts it sharply, in the King James Bible: "he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?" Then the Nazis took Paris.

teach.h: PAPERS, A HIDING PLACE, A CAMP.
teach.b: Jews were ordered to wear a yellow star, and her house became a hiding place.
With a priest of the house, Father Dimitri Klepinin, she gave Jews baptismal papers that might protect them, and helped hide people and get them out. The Gestapo arrested them both, and her son Yuri.
All three died in the camps. Mother Maria was sent to Ravensbrück, the camp where Betsie ten Boom died.

Some accounts say she took another woman's place in the line for the gas chamber; the sources are honest that nobody knows for sure. Orthodox Christians now honor her as a saint, with Father Dimitri and Yuri.

how: Orthodox Christians remember Saint Maria of Paris together with Father Dimitri Klepinin, her son Yuri and their companions, and her writings on love of neighbor are read in parishes and study groups.

games.q: you're a nun in occupied Paris. Jews are ordered to wear a yellow star, and some come to your door. what do you do?
o: pray for them, and send them on to someone else.
keep the house out of politics.
hide them and help them get papers.
games.why: Mother Maria's house became a hiding place, and with Father Dimitri she gave Jews baptismal papers that might protect them.

practice: Picture one person at risk right now, in your life or your news: someone sick, bullied, afraid of losing a home, far away in a war.
Look at that face the way Mother Maria looked at the person at her door, the way people look at an icon. If you pray, say the line from First John quietly.

wordCard.voice: Skobtsova. The Russian Orthodox nun in Paris who ran a house for the poor, helped Jews hide from the Nazis, and died at Ravensbrück.

orig.note: Greek: image, icon. Colossians 1:15 calls Christ the image of the invisible God.
